accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurately scoped. Acceptance, duplicate safety, dependency ordering and retained history do not imply completion, external atomicity or unlimited capacity. Both diagrams preserve these boundaries.

evidence.quote: That transaction protects its database effects. It does not make an external email or payment atomic, or turn delivery into a universal exactly-once guarantee.

mechanisms.reason: Actors and acknowledgements lead into the precise commit/crash gap and atomic duplicate record. Retry isolation, per-entity serial effects, backlog arithmetic and independent offsets expose state changes and failure responses for every card.

evidence.quote: In one database transaction, insert that ID into a durable processed-jobs table with a unique constraint and apply the job's database effect. Commit both or neither. A duplicate ID skips the effect. A separate check followed by a write can race or crash between steps.

coherence.reason: Deferred completion precedes producer/broker/worker flow, then crash recovery, ordering, overload and log comparison. Final request-boundary choice uses those costs; all eight card objectives and their prerequisite chains are taught.

evidence.quote: These acknowledgements cover different boundaries. Neither makes a broker operation atomic with a database write or proves an arbitrary business effect succeeded.

decisions.reason: Provides temporary versus terminal recovery, safe replay, hot-key serialization cost, bounded concurrency and visible producer control. Explains when synchronous authorization is necessary and independent retained history is useful.

evidence.quote: More workers help when workers are the bottleneck and downstream services have spare capacity. If the database is already saturated, more workers increase contention instead.

clarity.reason: Defines queue, workers, acknowledgements, idempotency, backpressure, partition and offset as used. Concrete crash, overwritten address and rate examples enable transfer without requiring a recurring story. Learner quotes are exact and entail all answers.

evidence.quote: In Kafka, a partition is an ordered slice of the log. Each group tracks its own position, called an offset, for each partition. Workers within a group share the partitions. Committing an offset records progress; it does not delete the event.

outcomes.reason: Maps API, broker and worker; confirmed configured handoff permits acceptance, saved result permits ready, acknowledgement retires delivery. Pending/ready/failed remain visible. Authorization dependency stays synchronous and status operation is a concrete cost. All six criteria follow slides 1,2,8.

Correctly traces committed credit before crash and possible redelivery; reversing acknowledgement creates lost-work window. Stable ID, durable unique record and credit share one transaction; duplicates skip effect. Explicitly limits protection to database effects, satisfying all five criteria.

Distinguishes temporary outage from unsupported input, delayed finite retries from terminal isolation, visible failure and continued healthy work. Cause correction and prior-effect inspection precede duplicate-safe replay. No arbitrary numeric retry setting required; all five criteria taught.

Transfers address race to inventory: late set-to-5 overwrites 2. Per-item serial effects include unfinished retries, different items remain parallel, hot item throughput is limited. All five criteria and dead-letter dependency caveat supported.

Computes 40 jobs/s; relates oldest age to completion delay; bounds saturated-store concurrency and explicitly throttles/rejects admissions. Finite buffering needs eventual catch-up; workers help only with worker bottleneck and downstream headroom. All six criteria supported.

Separates competing work from independently consuming groups, per-group partition offsets and shared partition work; progress does not delete retained events. One-day replay needs retained history; partition order and external-effect limits are explicit. All six criteria supported.

sourceChecks.claim: Verified asynchronous acknowledgement, status endpoint and separate result completion/failure in Microsoft pattern. Queue adds operational state and delays.

Verified RabbitMQ publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements are independent boundaries; latter permits deletion and cannot certify arbitrary effects. Diagram correctly orders broker acceptance, saved result/status and worker acknowledgement.

AWS explicitly requires stable caller identity and atomic token plus mutations. Unique durable ID plus database effect is a concrete application of that requirement; Kafka design also verifies post-effect/pre-progress crash redelivery. No external-effect atomicity claimed.

Microsoft retry verifies temporary/permanent distinction, increasing delays, finite attempts and idempotency. Supplement https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/competing-consumers verifies poison isolation; replay inspection follows the taught duplicate risk.

Competing-consumer source identifies ordering constraints and sessions. Supplement https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/message-sessions verifies exclusive per-session processing. Old write finishing last and blocking dependent effects through retries are logically correct application rules, not automatic broker guarantees.

Load-leveling source explicitly covers producer/consumer deficit, increased latency, bounded downstream rate, producer shedding and finite retention/quotas. 100 minus 70 equals 30; added workers cannot cure saturated downstream capacity.

Kafka design verifies per-group partition ownership, offsets, rewind and external-output coordination. Supplement https://kafka.apache.org/41/getting-started/introduction/ verifies consumption does not delete records, retention and partition ordering. Diagram accurately contrasts divided jobs with independent groups.

Microsoft pattern supports separate acceptance, pending/completed/failed states and status operation costs. Authorization must precede disclosure by the stated dependency; bounded overload follows slide 6, not an unconditional queue promise.
